claims.title: Finite nonconstant product laws and monotone count-tail bounds
claims.statement: Expand the actual independent nonconstant product weights to prove normalization, linearity, marginalization, disjoint-event factorization and the exact selected-coordinate identity. A finite three-state coupling and selected-subset union bound give both literal tail_le bounds for arbitrary q_i in [0,delta].
assumptions: Finite coordinate set and 0<=q_i<=delta<=1 for the probabilistic inequalities.
Conditioning is identified with the forced-coordinate law only when its selected-coordinate probability is positive; the underlying identity holds even when that probability is zero.

claims.title: Biased marked cells and the unchanged marked-tile constant
claims.statement: For probabilities in [3delta/4,delta], a length-u empty cell has probability at least (1-delta)^u and a singleton-even cell at least floor(u/2)*(3delta/4)*(1-delta)^(u-1). Disjoint cells yield literal markedLow. For u=ceil(1/delta), 0<delta<=1/100, prove the factors >=3/10 and >=891/8000>1/10, hence 10^(-(6r+1))<=markedLow<=1.
assumptions: Natural r>=0, u>=1 and the literal one-based cell-number/absolute-coordinate parity convention.
General finite lower bound needs 0<=delta<=1; the uniform numeric constant uses 0<delta<=1/100 and u=ceil_Nat(1/delta).

claims.title: Exact forced-point three-term bad-orbit estimate
claims.statement: Under (M+1)*(6r+1)*u<=n, forcing one coordinate gives bad-orbit probability at most n*choose(L2,K)*delta^K+n*(1-markedLow)^M+n*binUpper(G,delta,N-1). Cyclic complete-tile indices are distinct; remove at most one affected tile, leaving M independent tiles. The incomplete remainder and natural subtraction N-1 are treated explicitly.
assumptions: Natural n,L2,K,r,u,M,G,N,i0, u>=1, (M+1)*(6r+1)*u<=n, and probabilities in [3delta/4,delta] with 0<=delta<=1.
For the conditional-probability interpretation also i0<n and q_i0>0; the finite forced-law inequality does not divide by q_i0.

claims.title: Explicit uniform orbit_terms constants and threshold
claims.statement: For fixed eps>0 and real Co,Lb, use the actual KE,rE,dE,goodU,M,G,N. With theta=eps/8, h=2+8eps, pi0=10^(-(6r+1)), C1=(h+3)/pi0+2 and Cstar=2*(6r+1)*C1, take x0=exp(max(1,4*Cstar/theta^2,log(100)/theta)). Prove the tile-fit inequality and the entire source orbit_terms sum <=Cb*x^-2, where Cb=(|Co|+1)*((max(Lb,1))^K+2. Thus conditional bad probability is uniformly <=Cb*x^-2.
assumptions: x>=x0, natural n,L2 with x^(eps/4)<=n<=Co*x^(2+8eps) and L2<=Lb.
All constant choices precede x,n,L2, the probability profile, orbit base and forced coordinate. Impossible upper/lower ranges are vacuous.

claims.title: Literal ambient orbit identity and weighted selected-and-bad expectation
claims.statement: For a finite abelian group, an arbitrary step/base and a point in that based orbit, the injective order-n parametrization and finite marginalization give exactly P(point selected and based orbit bad)=q(point)*P_forced(bad). Applying BO4 gives <=delta*Cb*x^-2. Finite weighted summation yields E sum_p omega_p*bad_selected_count_p<=delta*|A|*Cb*x^-2*sum_p omega_p, with the t-dependent source selector allowed.
assumptions: Independent ambient probabilities q in [3delta/4,delta], x>=BO4 threshold, and every used step order in the BO4 interval.
For each step and point, the prescribed base b satisfies point=b+j*step for some natural j; b may depend on both inputs.
Finite step index set and nonnegative weights. No independence of the different bad-orbit events and no rotation invariance are assumed.
